note: ⛔ SNG-475. Mind's bargain craft. Every tradition should reach at least two of the four social verbs (SYSTEM_SPEC §31.5); Mind now has persuade, provoke, soothe and bargain.

abilities.name: Known Price
abilities.narrationHints: They let the other side name a figure, and then they name one, and the second figure is the one everybody uses. No haggling happens. It is faintly unnerving to watch.
abilities.description: Work out what the other side will actually accept before they say it — and open there, so the deal closes at your number instead of somewhere between.
abilities.notFor: Someone who does not want anything; a party you cannot observe or research; making them accept a price they cannot afford.

bounds.text: ⛔ THEY MUST WANT SOMETHING. A party with nothing to gain cannot be priced
⚠️ YOU MUST HAVE SOMETHING TO READ — a conversation, a ledger, a reputation, an hour in the same room. Cold, you get nothing
it tells you what they WILL take, never what they SHOULD — a bad deal correctly priced is still a bad deal
⚠️ someone who notices you never haggle stops negotiating with you in person

abilities.plainly: A social/investigate action that opens a negotiation at the closing figure. Its strength is rated 5 out of 10. Ranks: rank 2 finds what they would take instead, rank 3 finds the walk-away.

sectFlavour.syllogist: YOU REASONED IT — what a person in their position must need, and by when.
sectFlavour.cogitant: YOU MODELLED THEM — their pressures, their creditors, the thing they have not budgeted for.
sectFlavour.figurist: YOU READ THE SHAPE OF THE DEAL — every negotiation is an instance of a form, and forms have a settling point.

tree.name: Open at the Close
tree.grants: ⛔ NAME A FIGURE THEY WILL ACCEPT, FIRST. The deal closes at your number rather than halfway between two — no haggling round, no anchoring war, and you never overpay or insult them by lowballing.
tree.cannot: They must want something and you must have had something to read. It gives you their acceptable price, not a good one.

tree.name: What They Would Take Instead
tree.grants: ⚠️ ADDS SUBSTITUTION. Find the thing they would accept IN PLACE of what they asked for — passage instead of coin, a name instead of a favour, silence instead of either. ⛔ DEALS THAT WERE STUCK BECAUSE NEITHER SIDE HAD WHAT THE OTHER NAMED NOW CLOSE.
tree.cannot: The substitute must be something you can actually provide, and they must not already have it.

tree.name: Where They Walk
tree.grants: ⛔ ADDS THE WALK-AWAY. Know the point past which they leave the table — and know the one thing that would make them stay past it. ⚠️ You can push to the edge deliberately, or hand that edge to someone else to use.
tree.cannot: ⛔ Knowing the walk-away does not move it. Push past without the one thing, and they go, and they remember why.

abilities._authored:
⛔ SNG-475. `bargain` was zero corpus-wide until SNG-471 retagged nine crafts, and all nine sat in Demonic, Bargainers and Building. ⚠️ ERIK: 'bargain isn't only for Demonic and Bargainers — it's what ANY tradition would want to do because THERE IS AN ECONOMY.'
⛔ MIND'S LEVER IS KNOWING WHAT THE OTHER SIDE WILL ACCEPT BEFORE THEY SAY IT — which is a different craft from persuading them, and a different one again from the Bargainers' Honest Price, which states a cost rather than predicting acceptance.
⚠️ ASSESSMENT (§32.11): (1) opens the negotiation at the closing figure. (2) any deal where you have had an hour, a ledger or a reputation to read. (3) common — the game has an economy. (4) without it you haggle and land halfway. (5) r2 substitution, r3 walk-away. (6) the reasoning is flavour; the CLOSING PRICE is the mechanic.
